## Course Description ```{r child = here::here("fragments", "description.qmd")} ``` ## Prerequisites ```{r child = here::here("fragments", "prerequisites.qmd")} ``` # Learning Objectives ```{r child = here::here("fragments", "learning-objectives.qmd")} ``` # How the Course Works The course runs on a **dual spine**. Every week pairs: - **A workflow concept, taught hands-on in class.** Our 2.5-hour weekly session is a workshop. We learn a workflow skill by *doing it together* in real time — the first time you make a repository, open a pull request, or set up continuous integration, you'll do it live in class. - **An ambitious take-home build.** Each week's individual assignment is a build in an unfamiliar domain that forces you to apply that week's workflow skill on your own, at higher stakes. The sequence follows a **trust gradient**: we begin with high-touch, back-and-forth collaboration with an agent and progress toward orchestrating specialized agents that work for long stretches under your supervision. See the [schedule](schedule.qmd) for the week-by-week plan. # Assignments ## Participation & Attendance **Attendance will be taken and is the primary driver of your participation grade.** In-class work is hands-on and ungraded — but it is *practice for the build you do at home*. The take-home builds assume the skills we develop together in class, so missing class costs you twice: once on participation, and again on a much harder homework. Plan to attend in person every week. ## Individual Builds Each week (Weeks 1–8) you complete one **build**: an ambitious project in a domain you likely haven't worked in before. Each build is delivered as a **GitHub repository that includes the full conversation history** with the agent. Grading focuses on prompt quality, evidence of iterative collaboration, final product quality, and thoughtful use of the week's workflow skill. There are 8 builds, each worth 5% of your grade. ## Team Project Throughout the semester you'll work in **teams of 3–4** on an open-ended project of your own design — the one piece of fully open-ended work in the course. It is broken into milestone deliverables (proposal, interim report, final report, presentation). See the [project overview](project/0-overview.qmd) for details. # Grading Final grades will be calculated as follows:
Item | Weight | Notes -----|--------|---------------------------------- Individual Builds (8) | 40% | 8 builds, each worth 5% Team Project: Proposal | 5% | Teams of 3–4 (Week 6) Team Project: Interim Report | 10% | (Week 11) Team Project: Final Report | 25% | (Week 15) Final Presentation | 10% | (Week 16) Participation / Attendance | 10% | Yes, attendance is taken
## Generative-AI Use Policy Using AI agents is not "cheating" in this course — **it is the core skill being taught**. For individual builds you are *required* to use an agentic coding tool and to disclose your full conversation history as part of your submission. You remain fully responsible for the correctness, quality, and originality of everything you submit: read what the agent produces, run it, and fix it when it's wrong. Detailed disclosure requirements appear in each assignment. # Course Policies > *Detailed policies — late work, re-grades, academic integrity, attendance > thresholds, and university-required statements (DSS, religious holidays, CAPS, > nondiscrimination, recording) — will be merged in here from the working > syllabus draft (`class-factory.md`).*
